problem: The canonical DOC reader rejected older FIB versions only when the selected table stream was missing. A retained modern table stream caused older-profile headers to be misinterpreted as table pointers and reported as CLX corruption. Signature/trust rows also lacked native-parent operation coverage separating cryptographic validity, payload integrity, signature presence and PKI trust.
changes: Reject older DOC layouts before consulting modern table pointers, independently of table presence and stylesheet leniency. Retain the known C0 Word 97 shell-template exception; C2 compatibility admission is unchanged. Missing table streams on admitted modern profiles remain StreamNotFound.

Add two owning-DOC and one public-operations native-source derivative regressions for exact older-version refusals, compatible-header admission and error propagation. Originals are immutable and the derivatives are not claimed to be native-authored older Word files.

Add three signature regressions: caller-key signature creation/verification over seven native Office parents; signed workbook outer/inner no-op and edit policy through explicit unsign; and payload-tamper separation of integrity, signature math and trust.

Strengthen the existing tracked Microsoft Office 2010 certificate-bearing signature tests to require Trust::NotChecked. Add test-only P-256 and optional OPC signature-authoring dependencies for fixture creation; no production operations signing-provider API is introduced.

Replace two ignored DOC placeholders with a tracked native file-opening check and an in-memory typed invalid-CFB check. The tests no longer require an untracked test.doc or write test_invalid.tmp into the working directory.

Index six concrete native-input tests and record five explicit boundaries: doc-022, xls-196, xlsx-273, xlsb-339 and docx-132. Keep native-authored signed-fixture handoffs open and all historical authoring statuses unchanged.

verification_scope.legacy_admission: On native word-text-structure.doc and word-layout-extensions.dot derivatives, nFib 0021/0045/0065/0067/0068 yields exact UnsupportedVersion values/names under Strict and TolerateStylesheetDefects. Each retains 1Table. The positional edit owner returns Refused(UnsupportedSource). CFB envelopes are reserialized; all stream payloads except the selected WordDocument nFib bytes remain exact.
verification_scope.compatible_headers: C0 shell and C2 bidi derivatives retain complete projected text, 183 table pointers, template identity and byte-exact no-op publication. Their positional editing refusal matches the original rich-body restriction rather than becoming UnsupportedSource. This does not qualify all shell/bidi semantics or arbitrary FIB versions.
verification_scope.public_errors: Word 6/95 header derivatives of both native DOC/DOT parents return Code::UnsupportedFormat with nested DOC UnsupportedVersion through Auto/file and Eager/byte ingress. Original and temporary input files remain unchanged. The prior invalid-table-pointer interpretation is not accepted as the intended boundary.
verification_scope.seven_signature_parents: Native DOC/DOCX/PPT/PPTX text specimens and XLS/XLSX/XLSB metadata workbooks begin unsigned. Disposable deterministic caller-key XML signatures verify Valid integrity and signature math, Complete supported-resource reference coverage, non-SHA1 algorithms, exact claimed time, no certificate chain and Trust::NotChecked. Original CFB streams/data-part payloads remain exact; library reopen detects Signed, retains original text and publishes the signed archive exactly on no-op.
verification_scope.signed_edit_policy: XLS/XLSX/XLSB signed derivatives exercise Auto/file and Eager/byte ingress. Outer and wrapped inner handles retain cache A7=30 and exact no-op bytes and reject Z100 edits with DocumentProtected. Explicit unsign permits the edit. The result has no signatures and matches an ordinary native-source scalar edit by every CFB stream byte or the complete OPC content-type/relationship graph and every data-part payload. Other signed clones remain unchanged.
verification_scope.tamper_and_presence: Replacing only the signed Workbook or sheet1 payload with a valid scalar-edited payload makes integrity Invalid while signature math stays Valid and trust stays NotChecked. Opening still detects Signed because that wrapper is presence/edit-policy metadata, not automatic cryptographic verification. The original signed derivative continues to verify.
verification_scope.actual_microsoft_certificates: The pre-existing tracked Microsoft Office 2010 signed DOCX/XLSX/PPTX fixtures under test-data/poi/test-data/xmldsign have nonempty certificates and valid mathematical verification under their explicitly compatible SHA-1 policy, with Partial reference coverage and Trust::NotChecked. They supplement, rather than change, the 139-file corpus; no new native signatures were authored.
verification_scope.reactivated_tests: The raw DOC reader now opens the tracked native text fixture and asserts 183 pointers, 25 paragraphs and WORD_NATIVE_END. A zeroed 512-byte input asserts Error::Ole(NotOleFile) without filesystem side effects. Both former ignored placeholders now run.
verification_scope.limits: No native Word 6/95 interpretation, full C0/C2 compatibility, native-authored signature generation, fresh Office reopen, legacy CryptoAPI _signatures authoring, authenticated signer identity, certificate-chain/revocation lookup, trusted timestamp, macro execution or external activation is claimed. A mathematically valid signature is not PKI trust.
